title: Shape of paired cells depends on relative tensions at outer surface and partition

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Shape of paired cells depends on relative tensions at outer surface and partition

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Whether two adjacent cells in a filament (as in Nostoc and its allies) are separated by flat partitions, are hemispherical, or are each more than a hemisphere depends on the relative magnitudes of the tension at the outer cell surface and at the boundary between the cells.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: These various conditions depend, according to what we have already learned, upon the relative magnitudes of the tensions at the surface of the cells and at the boundary between them

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates”; topic “Two-celled aggregates and partition walls”. Scope: pairs and chains of cells in filamentous lower algae and other two-celled aggregates

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch07-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.63

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The force-balance relation makes quantitative, falsifiable geometric predictions. Public images permit tests in selected aggregates, although direct tension measurements and adequate taxonomic coverage are limited.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Infer relative interface tensions from contact angles in paired cells and test whether measured outer shape and partition curvature satisfy the force-balance equations.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cell walls and active growth can violate fluid-interface assumptions.

Nostoc and related taxa have limited suitable open 3D data.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Photographs can sort paired cells into the three curvature classes the claim names. They cannot supply the two tensions those classes are said to express, and treating curvature as a tension measurement makes the test circular. The shape catalogue is therefore only a partial check.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In filamentous cyanobacteria and similar pairs, class partition curvature as flat, hemispheric or more than hemispheric and, where possible, compare that class with measured tension at the outer surface and at the cell-cell boundary. The three shape classes tracking the three tension regimes would support the claim; shapes that stay flat across independently varied boundary tension would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Independent tension measurements in Nostoc and its allies are not part of these image archives.

Under a soap-film model the curvature is the tension ratio, so shape classes alone restate the claim.
